name: CA-39
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+7 district with well-funded incumbent Mark Takano seeking re-election
Republican Steve Manos reports no fundraising and draws no outside support
Prediction markets price a Democratic hold near 96 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; fundamentals carry the forecast
model.rationale: Takano combines a Democratic-leaning seat, a large financial edge, and zero outside spending against him, while Manos shows no visible campaign resources; markets price a near-certain Democratic hold, keeping the race Safe D with a slightly tempered margin.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Takano or a surprise Republican fundraising push would be the main signal that this race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mark Takano, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in this Riverside County-area district that leans Democratic by about seven points. He advanced to the general election and holds a large financial advantage, having raised roughly $894,000, while Republican Steve Manos reports no fundraising totals and has drawn no outside support. No outside groups are spending against Takano.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial edge, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at about 96 percent. The national environment adds a modest Democratic tilt. The seat remains Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any specific sign of vulnerability.
